mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 3% year-over-year signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or CPI YoY increases > 3% without subsequent tightening.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% signals a tightening labor market, leading to increased wage pressures and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as companies invest in productivity.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or UNRATE decreases below 4% without subsequent wage pressure.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% month-over-month signals increased economic activity and consumer confidence, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or HOUST increases > 5% MoM without subsequent economic activity.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) by more than 0.5% in a quarter signals a tightening monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or FEDFUNDS increases > 0.5% without subsequent tightening.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% month-over-month signals increased economic output and supply-side strength, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or INDPRO increases > 1% MoM without subsequent economic output.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) by more than 1% month-over-month signals a decline in consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or RSAFS decreases > 1% MoM without subsequent demand decline.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 month-over-month signals strong job growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending increases.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or PAYEMS increases > 200,000 MoM without subsequent consumer spending.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the GDP (GDPC1) growth rate is below 2% year-over-year, it signals a restrictive monetary policy in a low-growth environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: restrictive monetary policy in low-growth environment
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the combination of high FEDFUNDS and low GDPC1 growth does not lead to negative returns.
